title: Hand hygiene and personal protective equipment
audience: Cleaners and cleaning supervisors working between resident rooms and other areas of residential aged care, clinics, dental practices and NDIS settings in any Australian state or territory.
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: NHMRC, Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare (2019) (no page date shown); NDIS Practice Standards and Quality Indicators, Version 4 (November 2021), Core Module (no page date shown). Only part of each of these sources has been confirmed.
learningOutcomes: Describe the hand hygiene points a cleaner passes through between rooms, using the facility's sequence.
Choose and use protective equipment for a room task in line with the facility assessment and product safety data sheet.
Prevent cross-contamination between resident rooms by controlling gloves, cloths and equipment.
Stop and report when protection is missing, damaged or contaminated, and record the event.

instruction.heading: Why hand hygiene is the first control
instruction.body: Hands are the most common way that organisms move from one surface or person to another. A cleaner touches door handles, handrails, call bells, equipment and clean stock many times in a shift, and each touch can carry an organism to the next place. The NDIS Practice Standards and Quality Indicators, Version 4 of November 2021, require that standard precautions are implemented in settings where supports are provided, and that workers are trained in hand hygiene and respiratory hygiene. The NHMRC Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare (document dated 2019) set the national framework. Hand hygiene is not a single action; it is a practice at the points where the risk changes.

instruction.heading: The transition points in a resident room
instruction.body: Perform hand hygiene at the points the facility specifies. In a typical resident room these include before entering the room, after removing gloves, after any contact with a resident's body fluid or their immediate surroundings, after touching a shared surface where the facility requires it, and before touching clean stock or leaving the room. A common failure is to clean a bedside table with gloves and then open a clean supply cupboard. The gloves must be removed, hand hygiene performed, and new gloves put on before the clean supply is touched. Follow the facility sequence, not habit.

instruction.heading: Choosing protection for the room task
instruction.body: Select protective equipment from the facility's task assessment and the product safety data sheet, as set out in the medical equipment cleaning lesson on PPE and hand hygiene. Gloves are chosen for the task and the product, not for the room. A task that involves a spill, body fluid, or a sharp needs the protection the facility specifies for that task, and the cleaner does not decide to use less because the spill looks small. Check gloves and other protection before each use, and replace any that are torn, contaminated or the wrong type. Where the facility provides a gown, mask or eye protection for a room, follow the notice or instruction for that room.

instruction.heading: Preventing cross-contamination between rooms
instruction.body: Cross-contamination happens when something dirty touches something clean. Keep one room's cloths, gloves and waste out of the next room. Do not use the same cloth in more than one room unless the facility's procedure allows it, and do not carry used cloths in your pocket or on the trolley's clean shelf. Work from the area the facility's procedure directs as least contaminated to most contaminated, and keep used items in a closed container until they reach the holding area. A cloth used in a bathroom placed on a clean trolley shelf is a cross-contamination event to be stopped and reported.

instruction.heading: Exposure and stop-work
instruction.body: If your protection tears, you touch a body fluid with bare skin, or you are exposed through a splash or a sharp, stop the task, remove yourself from the immediate area, and follow the facility's exposure procedure. Report to the nurse in charge or supervisor the same shift. Do not continue a room because the protection was only slightly damaged. Stop work when the required protection is not available, and record the event and the decision. The facility, not the cleaner, decides any follow-up for an exposure.

procedure: Check the room notice and the facility task assessment, and select protection for the task.
Perform hand hygiene before entering the room, and put on the selected protection in the facility's order.
Complete the task in the facility's sequence, keeping clean supplies away from used items.
Perform hand hygiene and change gloves at each transition the facility specifies, including before touching clean stock.
Remove protection in the reverse order at the room exit, and perform hand hygiene.
If protection is torn or contaminated, or an exposure occurs, stop, follow the exposure procedure, and report the same shift.
Record the protection used, any exposure or stop, the person told and the time.

workedExamples.situation: You clean a resident's bedside table with gloves on, then open the clean supply cupboard in the corridor with the same gloves, and then enter the next room.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must you do, and what should be recorded?
workedExamples.reasoning: The gloves have touched a surface in a room and then clean stock. Stop, remove the gloves, perform hand hygiene, put on new gloves, and check that the clean stock is not contaminated. If the clean stock was touched, tell the supervisor so the facility decides whether it is set aside. Record the event as a near-miss for review.

workedExamples.situation: A resident's room notice requires gown and eye protection for a task, but the trolley holds only gloves and a mask.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The protection the notice requires is not available, so the task cannot start as directed. Do not substitute. Tell the nurse in charge, postpone the task, and record the reason and the time.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves selected for the task and product: {{business:safety.required_ppe}}
Gown, mask or eye protection as specified by the room notice or task assessment
Hand hygiene products provided by the facility

commonErrors.error: Touching clean stock or a shared handle with the gloves used in a room.
commonErrors.prevention: Remove gloves, perform hand hygiene, and put on new gloves at each transition.

commonErrors.error: Using the same cloth in several rooms to save time.
commonErrors.prevention: Use cloths as the facility procedure allows. Keep used cloths in a closed container.

commonErrors.error: Continuing a task with damaged protection because the damage seems minor.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, replace the protection or stop the task, and report the damage.

commonErrors.error: Using less protection than a room notice requires because the task looks simple.
commonErrors.prevention: Follow the notice exactly. Postpone the task if the required protection is not available.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The NDIS Practice Standards and Quality Indicators, Version 4 of November 2021, Core Module, require that standard precautions are implemented in settings where supports are provided. They require training in standard precautions, hand hygiene, respiratory hygiene and cough etiquette, and training in PPE use for each worker who provides direct support, with PPE available to each worker who needs it.
The NHMRC Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare (2019) provide the national framework for hand hygiene and PPE.

Licence notice: Completing this lesson does not grant any authority to handle clinical waste, sharps or regulated body fluids. Those tasks are outside this lesson and require facility authorisation and any state or territory requirement that applies.

qualityStandard: The learner names the hand hygiene points between two supplied rooms, in the facility sequence, with none missed.
The learner selects protection for three supplied room tasks from the notice and the safety data sheet, and states the reason for each.
The learner identifies and corrects a cross-contamination event in a supplied scenario, and records it.
The learner stops and reports a supplied exposure in order, without continuing the task.
documentationEvidence: Protection used for each room task, and any substitution or shortfall
Any cross-contamination event or exposure, with time, action taken and person notified
Any task postponed because required protection was not available
summary: Hand hygiene is performed at the facility's transition points, including between rooms and before clean stock.
Protection is chosen from the room notice, the task assessment and the safety data sheet, and never reduced.
Keep cloths, gloves and waste out of the next room, and stop any cross-contamination event.
After an exposure or damaged protection, stop, report the same shift, and record the event.

knowledgeChecks.question: After cleaning a bedside table with gloves on, what must you do before touching the clean supply cupboard?
options: Wipe the gloves on your uniform and continue the task
Nothing, because the cupboard is in the corridor away from the room
Remove the gloves, perform hand hygiene, and put on new gloves.

knowledgeChecks.question: A room notice requires gown and eye protection, but only gloves and a mask are on the trolley. What should you do?
options: Do not start. Tell the nurse in charge, postpone the task, and record the reason.
Start the task with the gloves and mask, since they are close enough.
Use a plastic apron instead of the gown to complete the task.

knowledgeChecks.question: Your protection is torn during a task and you may have touched a body fluid. What is the correct action?
options: Finish the task, then report at the end of the shift, once the room is fully clean
Stop, follow the facility exposure procedure, and report to the supervisor the same shift.
Replace the protection and carry on without telling anyone, since it was only a small contact
